description: Implement User Order History with view, filter, and reorder functionality. Users can see their past orders with details, filter by status, and reorder items. This provides transparency and improves user experience for repeat purchases.
steps: Add getUserOrders(userId) function to database.js that filters getOrders() by userId and returns sorted by createdAt descending
Add 'My Orders' button to user menu in index.html topbar next to logout button, styled like admin-switch class

Create order history modal in index.html with structure: modal-head with title 'My Orders', filter tabs (All/Pending/Processing/Delivered/Cancelled), orders list container, close button. Use existing modal styles.

In app.js, add event listener for 'My Orders' button that calls renderOrderHistory() and shows modal. Function should call getUserOrders(), render order cards showing order ID, date (formatted), items list, total, status badge (reuse existing .status classes), and 'Reorder' button per order.
Implement filter functionality: add click handlers to status filter buttons that re-render order list filtered by selected status. Use .active class toggle like category tabs.
Implement reorder functionality: 'Reorder' button handler that reads order.items, populates cart with those items, calls updateCartCount(), shows success toast, and closes order history modal.
Add empty state message when user has no orders: 'You haven't placed any orders yet. Start shopping!'
Wire up close button with data-close attribute following existing modal pattern
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated users see 'My Orders' button in topbar next to logout
Clicking 'My Orders' opens modal showing all user's orders sorted newest first
Each order card displays: order ID, date, item count, total amount, status badge
Filter tabs work: clicking 'Pending' shows only pending orders, etc.
Clicking 'Reorder' on any order adds all items to cart and shows success toast
Empty state appears when user has no orders
verification: Open index.html in browser, register and login as new user
Place 2-3 test orders with different items
Click 'My Orders' button - modal should open showing all orders
Test each filter tab - verify correct orders appear
Click 'Reorder' on an order - verify items added to cart and cart count updates
Test with user who has no orders - verify empty state appears
findings: Implementation complete. All features working as expected: getUserOrders function added to database.js, My Orders button added to topbar, order history modal created with filter tabs, renderOrderHistory function implemented, filter functionality working with active state toggle, reorder functionality adds items to cart and shows toast, empty state message displays correctly, modal close button wired with data-close attribute. Styles added for order-filter-tabs, order-history-list, order-card, and reorder-button following existing design patterns.
